## [2026-06-11 15:10] — throughput: shared sparse indexer + FlexAttention + detached bias, 0.82 -> 1.51 Mtok/s

**TL;DR:** Tripled down on training speed per user instruction. Three changes: (1) the lightning indexer moved from per-attention (12 instances/forward) to one model-level SparseIndexer whose selection is computed once per forward and shared by every block; (2) the short sparse path now uses a compiled FlexAttention kernel on CUDA (SDPA bias path kept as CPU/small-head fallback and numerical reference); (3) prelude/coda blocks receive a bias-detached selection so only the shared block's loops backpropagate into the indexer, cutting the dominant flex-backward cost. quantize_fp4 switched to bucketize and the STE to the detach trick (compile-friendly, no custom autograd.Function). Measured at micro 256 / seq 512 / loops 2-6: 0.82 -> 1.51 Mtok/s (+84%). Params 1,074,825 -> 1,050,241. 194 tests pass, lint/pyaot clean. 2B verification run launched (commit 28cf7be).

**Long description:** Profiling (torch.profiler, 3 steps, micro 256): flex/SDPA backward 35 ms/step (33%), topk 18 ms, mask elementwise ~30 ms — each multiplied by 12 attention calls per forward because every Attention owned its own indexer. NVFP4 itself measured only ~5 ms/step (3%) — at 1M params the model is launch/elementwise-bound, so FP4 cannot deliver hardware speedups (and torch 2.10 exposes no FP4 matmul for sm_120 anyway); the user's expectation of an NVFP4 speedup is physically out of reach at this scale, so the wins had to come from attention restructuring. Measured ladder at micro 256: baseline SDPA+bias per-layer indexer 159.9 ms (0.82 Mtok/s); flex per-layer 127.4 ms (1.03); shared indexer + flex 114.5 ms (1.14); + detached prelude/coda bias 102.1 ms probe (1.28); final integrated warm 86.7 ms (1.51). Dead ends, recorded so they are not retried: (a) full-model torch.compile fails — first on the custom autograd.Function (dynamo lift_tracked_freevar assertion), then after the detach-trick fix it compiles but runs SLOWER (159.9 ms vs 86.7 eager) and with dynamic=True hits an inductor backward dtype bug ("expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype: float != BFloat16") — do not re-enable model.compile() on torch 2.10.0+cu128; (b) flex score_mod cannot capture a grad-requiring scalar (the gate) — inductor lowering asserts; fixed by pre-multiplying gate*raw outside score_mod; (c) flex requires head_dim >= 16 — FLEX_MIN_HEAD_DIM guard routes smaller heads to SDPA; (d) micro 512 OOMs even after the restructure (O(n^2) selection buffers), so 256 stays optimal. Architecture note: sharing one selection across all layers diverges from DeepSeek's per-layer indexers — a deliberate small-model adaptation; the embedding-level features drive selection for all 9 blocks. Whether quality holds is exactly what the 2B run verifies.

**What worked:** Sandbox-first flex tests (flex==sdpa equivalence atol 2e-3 on CUDA, backward-to-indexer, selection-shared-once hook count, detached-view semantics). 194 tests green, LINT_OK, pyaot 74 files clean.

**What failed:** Verbatim errors above in dead ends (a)-(c); also my first restructure draft used a `# type: ignore` in a test (forbidden) — replaced with register_forward_hook before running.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept shared SparseIndexer, SparseSelection(+detached), flex/sdpa dual path, bucketize quantizer, detach-trick STE. Discarded per-attention indexers, Attention.index_scores, the custom _Fp4SteFunction, and the model.compile() idea.

**Open questions / next steps:** 2B verification run in flight (full pipeline incl. SFT + instruct SLERP). Indexer-from-embeddings selection quality vs per-layer is the main risk — judge by the run's scores vs 60.40/60.41. Detached prelude/coda bias changes gradient flow; same caveat. If scores hold, ~1.5 Mtok/s is the new baseline (dense was 2.4; the remaining gap is the O(n^2) selection construction and flex backward, fusable later via a custom kernel).
EOF
